content.key_idea: When the true bottleneck edge (A-B's background traffic) already fixes the optimal MLU, the remaining demand can be split across alternate paths in more than one way, evenly (balanced) or skewed onto a single path (imbalanced), without changing the achieved MLU.
content.reading_order: system information (a) gives u*, demand, and which paths carry flow; background traffic (b) fixes the shared black-edge values; Solution 1 (c) and Solution 2 (d) then overlay two different red/orange splits on the same graph, with the green direct-path value unchanged

style.stroke: thin (~0.44pt) black outlines for the table and node circles/background edges; coloured strokes for each overlay path
style.arrows: thin black arrows for background traffic; coloured arrows (green/red/orange) overlaid on the same or adjacent edges for the SD-specific path split, with a curved green arrow for the direct path

encoding.color_means: green marks the direct A-B path's share of the (A,B) demand (T_ABB), red marks the A-C-B path's share (T_ACB), orange marks the A-D-B path's share (T_ADB); black marks fixed background traffic from other demands
encoding.line_style_means: a curved green arrow distinguishes the direct-path overlay from the straight black background edge it runs alongside; red and orange overlays follow the same straight edges as the background but in their own colour
encoding.state_means: the two alternatives are told apart by the numeric split on the red and orange paths, even (0.5/0.5) in Solution 1 versus skewed (1/0) in Solution 2, while every background value and the green path stay identical
encoding.marker_means: no numbered markers; each edge's 'used/capacity' fraction is both its label and its value
encoding.emphasis: keeping every black background number and the green path identical between (c) and (d) isolates the red/orange numbers as the only thing that changed, making the multi-solution phenomenon visually obvious
reusable_patterns: a shared background graph redrawn twice with only two coloured path variables' split changed, so the reader can see two different feasible solutions reach the same bottleneck value
weaknesses: stacking two numeric labels (background and overlay) on the same short edge segment makes the diagram dense and requires matching each number's colour carefully to its path

summary: This figure illustrates SSDO's multi-solution phenomenon: for the same optimal maximum link utilization (u*=0.8), more than one split-ratio solution for the (A,B) demand (D_AB=1) is feasible. System information (a) and background traffic (b) fix a 4-node graph (A, B, C, D) with black background flows, including A-B already at 1.6/2. Solution 1 (c) splits the (A,B) demand's remaining routing evenly across two indirect paths, A-C-B (red, 0.5/2 on each leg) and A-D-B (orange, 0.5/2 on each leg), with the direct path unused (green, 0/2); this is the balanced solution the paper's binary search finds. Solution 2 (d) reaches the same optimal MLU by instead routing the full demand through A-C-B (red, 1/2 on each leg) while leaving A-D-B unused (orange, 0/2); it is feasible but fails the balance condition since the A-D-B path's utilization stays below the required threshold.
summary_zh: 该图示SSDO多解现象：(A,B)需求可用不同分流达到同一最优MLU。(c)方案一均分给A-C-B、A-D-B两条间接路径（各0.5/2），为均衡解；(d)方案二全走A-C-B（各1/2），A-D-B为0，同达最优但不均衡。
notes: content.elements' T_ABB/T_ACB/T_ADB values (0/1/1 in the table) are interpreted as which paths carry nonzero flow in the balanced solution (c), not literal flow amounts, since the actual per-solution numeric splits (0.5/0.5 vs 1/0) are read directly off the (c)/(d) overlay labels; this interpretation follows the paper's Characteristic 3 text ('fACB and fADB are greater than zero') rather than being stated outright. layout.panel_count/panels=4 matches the index's own (2x2) count, with content.panels listing only (c)/(d) as the comparison pair while (a)/(b) are shared setup panels.
